decisions.reason: The firm has publicly promoted this webservice and it builds on established offerings, so escalation pressures favor continuing rather than writing off the investment.
As a database close to the core business with a dedicated public page, it represents a committed offering whose sunk costs and visibility make dropping less likely.
The service is close to the firm's established regulatory/energy processes and has been publicly committed, so escalation logic suggests persistence.
The end-customer tariff database is a multi-model product line, implying higher investment and centrality, which strongly favors keeping it under escalation of commitment.

Custom web services are building on existing capabilities and were publicly announced, but their less standardized nature gives a moderate probability of discontinuation; still, sunk and public commitment keep it on the market.
The postal code lookup service is a public, established add-on, but its generic character makes it somewhat more droppable than core data products; escalation still favors keeping for now.
